# Rename `verify.overlap_enabled` → `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`, with a permanent alias and a docs entry

## Context / Problem

`verify.overlap_enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:140`) turns on a store-wide, LLM-backed
cross-ticket duplicate detector that runs during `review-plan`. The name says none of the four
things an operator needs at the config line: overlap of *what*, that retrieval scans the *whole*
tracker so the work scales with store size, that it is *advisory* and can never block, and that it
rides on `review-plan`. Sitting under `verify.` next to genuinely blocking gates
(`require_plan_review_for_claim`, `require_ticket_for_commit`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:133,144`)
it actively reads as a gate.

**The documentation gap is the concrete half of the defect, and it is narrower than first reported.**
Grepping the tree: `docs/config.md` contains **zero** occurrences of the string `overlap` — so the
key has no entry in the config-key inventory that operators actually read. The single mention
anywhere in `docs/` is one bullet in an architecture decision record,
`docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md:64`. For an opt-in feature that spends LLM tokens
proportional to tracker size, that is the part most likely to cost someone money or confusion. This
repo itself runs with it on (`rebar.toml:39`), so the rename must not break a live config.

## Approach

Rename the field to **`verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`**, keep both the old TOML key and the old
env var working forever as **permanent aliases**, and add the missing `docs/config.md` entry. The
name states the *output* — link suggestions — which is the thing an operator is deciding whether
they want, and the `suggest_` prefix carries the advisory nature that `_enabled` does not. It fits
because the whole complaint is that the name describes an internal mechanism ("overlap") instead of
a user-visible product, and the config inventory is read by operators, not by the retrieval code.

### Why permanent, not scheduled

The deprecation registry records the deciding rule in prose at `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:88-99`:
the six `_permanent` entries above it are permanent **because they are RENAMES** — "the same knob
under a better name, so removing them would buy nothing" — while `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is `_scheduled`
because it is a **supersession by a different interface**. This change is a pure rename: same
boolean, same default, same consumers, better name. So both new rows use `_permanent(...)`
(`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:65`), which also picks the right message wording — `_message()`
(`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:299-306`) emits "is a permanent alias of …" and never claims
"deprecated", the contradiction the registry docstring was written to resolve.

### Backward compatibility rides on machinery that already exists

Both alias paths are already built and already tested; this change supplies data, not mechanism.

**TOML key.** `_ALIASES` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:645`) is an **empty** `dict[str, dict[str, str]]`
kept explicitly as "the extension point for any future config-key rename window". `coerce_sparse`
consumes it at `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:689-695`: for each `old → new` pair present in a
section it calls `warn_deprecated(f"cfg:{sect}.{old}")` and rewrites the key, and if the canonical
key is *also* present the canonical wins and the legacy one is dropped. So the entire TOML
back-compat is one line — `_ALIASES = {"verify": {"overlap_enabled": "suggest_duplicate_tickets"}}` —
plus the registry row whose key must be exactly `cfg:verify.overlap_enabled`, because that is the
string `coerce_sparse` builds and `warn_deprecated` raises `KeyError` on an unregistered key
(`src/rebar/_deprecations.py:329`).

**Env var.** The canonical name is derived mechanically as `REBAR_<SECTION>_<KEY>`, so it changes
from `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` to `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS`. `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`
(`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:295-315`) maps `legacy → (section, key, canonical)`, and
`env_overrides` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:340-343`) honours the legacy name **only when the
canonical key is unset in that layer**, warning through `warn_deprecated(f"env:{legacy}")`.
`_map_legacy_env` needs **no** change: it special-cases only `REBAR_NO_SYNC` and
`REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE` and returns the value unchanged otherwise
(`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:319-326`). The config-cache signature already iterates
`_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` (`src/rebar/config.py:279-280`), so a mid-process change to the legacy var
correctly invalidates the cache with no extra work.

Worked example of the two contracts, the thing a reviewer should be able to check by eye:

```toml
# an existing project config — keeps working, emits one permanent-alias notice
[tool.rebar.verify]
overlap_enabled = true              # → resolves to verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets = True

# both set — the canonical key wins, the legacy one is dropped without a warning
overlap_enabled          = false
suggest_duplicate_tickets = true    # → resolves to True
```

```sh
REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1 rebar review-plan <id>          # honored, warns
REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1 \
  REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS=0 rebar review-plan <id>   # canonical wins → off
```

### The three call sites, and one correction to this ticket's own file-impact

Grepping `src/rebar` for `overlap_enabled` returns exactly four hits: the field declaration
(`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:140`), its `_SECTIONS` coercer (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:528`), and
two readers — `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:233` (the opportunistic enrichment drain's feature gate
on ticket-write paths) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:765` (the advisory step inside the
plan review, with its explanatory comment at `:755-761`). **`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`
does not reference the flag** — this ticket's previous file-impact list named it in error, and it is
dropped. `src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py` is also **not** edited: `overlap_findings`
(`src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py:23`) never reads the flag, it is merely what the flag guards.

### Scope boundary held deliberately

The `[tool.rebar.llm]` tunables `overlap_k` / `overlap_drain` / `overlap_conf_threshold` and friends
(`src/rebar/llm/config.py:428-445`) keep their names. They live on `LLMConfig`, a different section
with a different audience (they tune the algorithm, they do not decide whether the feature runs),
and renaming eleven tunables would turn a one-key rename into a migration. The new `docs/config.md`
entry cross-references them by their existing names instead.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — rename the field at line 140 and its explanatory comment at
  lines 134-139; rename the `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer key at line 528; populate `_ALIASES` at
  line 645 with the one `verify` entry.
- `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — two `_permanent` rows in `_ENTRIES` (`:73`): `cfg:verify.overlap_enabled`
  and `env:REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED`.
- `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — one `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` entry (`:295-315`).
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — the read at line 233.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py` — the read at line 765 and the comment naming the flag at
  line 759.
- `rebar.toml` — this repo's own setting at line 39 and its comment block at lines 32-38.
- `docs/config.md` — the new inventory entry in the `[tool.rebar]` verify block (the block at
  lines 93-110), plus the new permanent env rename added to the Back-compat list at lines 409-419,
  which today enumerates the six permanent renames.
- `docs/adr/0037-cross-ticket-overlap.md` — line 64 names the old key; it gains the new name so the
  record stays navigable. The ADR's decision text is otherwise left intact, because an ADR records
  what was decided at the time.
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — add `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` (near line 45) and
  `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS` (near line 96); the existing `verify.overlap_enabled`
  (line 45) and `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` (line 96) entries **stay**, because the golden is an
  anti-regression record of surfaces that must remain accounted for.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py` — the four schema assertions at lines 58-60 and 262-265.
- `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py` — the attribute set at line 176 and the comment at line 58.
- `tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py` (new) — the alias behaviour.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py`:

- **Happy path (TOML alias)** — `coerce_sparse({"verify": {"overlap_enabled": "true"}})` returns
  `{"verify": {"suggest_duplicate_tickets": True}}`, so an untouched project config still turns the
  feature on.
- **Happy path (env alias)** — with `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1` and the canonical var unset,
  `env_overrides()` yields `{"verify": {"suggest_duplicate_tickets": "1"}}`.
- **Conflict / precedence edge** — with **both** the legacy and canonical TOML keys present the
  canonical value wins and no warning is emitted; with both env vars set the canonical wins. These
  are the two cases the `coerce_sparse` and `env_overrides` code paths branch on and the two a naive
  alias gets backwards.
- **Empty / absent edge** — with neither set, `Config` resolves `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets`
  to `False`, proving the default did not move.
- **Message wording** — `warn_deprecated("cfg:verify.overlap_enabled")` returns a string containing
  "permanent alias" and **not** "scheduled for removal", pinning the `_permanent` classification
  rather than just asserting the row exists.

Regression suites this change can break, run explicitly:
`tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` (its alias accounting at lines 47-56 and 62-70 is what
makes the golden tolerate the renamed key), `tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py` (registry
completeness plus the raw-emission source scan), `tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py`,
`tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`, and `tests/unit/test_config_show.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is the canonical boolean (default `False`) on
      `VerifyConfig` with its `_SECTIONS["verify"]` coercer, and `verify.overlap_enabled` is no
      longer a live key; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review_overlap.py` (whose assertions at lines 58-60 and 262-265
      pin exactly the field, the `_SECTIONS` membership and the coercer).
- [ ] An existing project config setting `overlap_enabled = true` still turns the feature on and
      emits a permanent-alias notice; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_toml_alias_resolves`.
- [ ] `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1` still turns the feature on when the canonical var is unset;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_env_alias_resolves`.
- [ ] When legacy and canonical are both set — in TOML or in the environment — the canonical value
      wins; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_canonical_wins_over_legacy`.
- [ ] Both alias rows exist in `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` with `permanent=True` and
      `remove_in is None`, and their message says "permanent alias" rather than "scheduled for
      removal"; verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_config_alias_overlap_rename.py::test_rows_are_permanent` and by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_deprecation_registry.py`, which additionally fails if any emission
      site bypasses `warn_deprecated`.
- [ ] The two in-source readers (`src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:233`,
      `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:765`) and this repo's own `rebar.toml:39` use the new
      name, and the only surviving occurrences of the old name are the four back-compat sites.
      The grep must be **case-insensitive**, because two of the four spell the name in upper case
      (the env var) and two in lower case (the TOML key) — a case-sensitive `grep "overlap_enabled"`
      would silently miss the env-alias sites and make this criterion pass while they were wrong.
      So: `grep -rni "overlap_enabled" src rebar.toml` returns exactly these four lines and nothing
      else —
      (1) the `_ALIASES` entry `"overlap_enabled": "suggest_duplicate_tickets"` in
      `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`;
      (2) the `_permanent("cfg", "verify.overlap_enabled", …)` row in `src/rebar/_deprecations.py`;
      (3) the `_permanent("env", "REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED", …)` row in the same file;
      (4) the `"REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED"` key of `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` in
      `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`.
      In particular `grep -rni "overlap_enabled" rebar.toml` returns **zero** lines. Verified by
      running those two greps and by `pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` documents the setting: what it produces (up to three advisory
      `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`depends_on` link suggestions), its three stages — the query
      ticket's digest via `enrich`, BM25F retrieval over the whole tracker with the query's own
      graph excluded, then a bounded pairwise LLM judge (`src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py:41-56`) —
      that it is advisory and NEVER blocks a claim or close, that its cost scales with tracker size
      rather than with the reviewed ticket, and that the algorithm tunables are the
      `[tool.rebar.llm] overlap_*` keys. The entry deliberately does **not** pin a per-stage model
      class, since that routing is being changed by bug `afeb`. Verified by
      `grep -n "suggest_duplicate_tickets" docs/config.md` returning the new entry and by reading
      that the five listed facts are present.
- [ ] The new permanent env rename `REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED` →
      `REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS` is listed in the Back-compat section of
      `docs/config.md` alongside the six existing permanent renames (lines 409-419); verified by
      `grep -n "REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS" docs/config.md`.
- [ ] No config surface is orphaned by the rename: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` carries both
      the old and new key and both env names, and the old ones are accounted for as aliases;
      verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and no file in `src/rebar` exceeds the module-size cap;
      verified by the CI module-size gate.
